# A finite graph rule for joint slow-source repayment

Author synthesis. This is a conditional, checkable episode criterion with a completed six-species instance in BALANCED_NORMAL_CELL_PHYSICAL_EPISODE.md. It is not a theorem that every weakly reversible raw list has the required policy or reference barrier. It does not supply a global boundary receiver for free.

## 1. A bounded packet potential fixes the receiving contract

Let a finite auxiliary mode set M have fixed integer packet vectors tau_p. Let ell have strictly positive coordinates and define n=ell.(x-tau_p). Choose a fixed C so z=n+C>=1 at every admitted physical/mode state. The common receiver is U=D z^p; it is normlike because the packet set is bounded. Every raw reaction is counted ONCE: assign it either a normal mode update or an unexpected exit update. All chosen updates must be valid at their actual physical outputs.

Require each normal update to keep n fixed. At a fixed normal cell, positive ell and finite modes imply finite physical state space; extra conserved lattice coordinates can split it further. All unexpected updates have bounded |Delta n|<=B, directly from the finite raw and packet lists. Thus the receiver is acquired globally from finite data, even at outputs for which no return policy has yet been proved.

The six-species instance dispenses with auxiliary ambiguity: tau depends on actual capped anchors, its count is m(A)+m(D), and ell=1.

## 2. Acquiring a normal reference is a finite identity problem

A useful ansatz on a translated conservative fiber is

    mu(x,p)=a_p chi(residual)/x!,

where chi has fixed edge ratios along the conservative lattice. Substitute every NORMAL raw mass-action channel into mu Q=0. Multiplying a channel propensity by 1/x! leaves kappa/(x-source)!. Terms with the same residual background must balance. Equality of those finite background/mode coefficients gives a finite linear system in the a_p (and explicit conservative edge-ratio compatibility conditions).

Finding a positive solution and checking every background group acquires an invariant normal reference measure. Failure of this ansatz is a scoped refusal, not instability. A normal reference is not an equilibrium law of the physical entrance or of a surviving trajectory. # A constructive productive-exit synthesis rule

The new star launch suggests a reusable operation, rather than an enlarged ordered-cycle constant. This statement is a proof rule, not a claim that every weakly reversible list has its certificate.

Fix one proper receiving quantity z>=1 whose normal transitions are neutral, and whose genuine stopped increments are bounded. Partition a complete actual launch's exits into direct repayment G, harmful B, neutral C, clean activation A and other neutral U. Suppose its RAW finite mode flow acquires

    P_B<=C_B P_A,
    P_C+P_U<=C_0 P_A,
    E launch_time<=C z^s.

Every exit is included, so P_G+P_A>=p_*>0. A harmful launch need not have vanishing probability. The key is a proved matching of its actual flux to an activation opportunity, before receiving those outputs. Such a matching can be acquired by finite crossing potentials and exact raw propensity ratios, as in the seven-state star; it is not an assumption of an exit profile.

For each clean activation input, PERSONALLY construct a continuation at the same z, including its failures, with

    E Delta z <=-L d+o(1),
    E(Delta z)^2<=C_L,
    E continuation_time<=C_L z^s.

Require a fixed bound on each continuation's final increment (or prove all higher moments needed by a chosen power). An activation kernel or expectation supplied without its physical construction does not satisfy this requirement. In the completed instance it is actual quartic core hitting, paid noncore interruption, followed by a fixed number of actual normal-cell episodes whose finite adjoint occupation and raw crossing debt comparison are proved.

If launch increments satisfy Delta z<=-a on G, <=b on B and <=0 elsewhere, choose the fixed L with Ld>b C_B+a. Then the complete actual episode has

    E Delta z <=-a(P_G+P_A)+o(1)<=-a p_*/2,
    E(Delta z)^2<=C,
    E episode_time<=C z^s.

An integer power p>=max(2,s+1), with a fixed scalar multiplier, pays physical time by the SAME receiving function z^p. When s=1 the receiver is quadratic. This uses bounded increments at the final actual stop; it does not require exponential return, a bounded word length, stationary activity or a uniform fiber gap.
